Read docs/TASK_P31c_scope.md sections 1 (Design), 2.2 (src/rules/guardrails.ts) and 4. Patch src/rules/guardrails.ts (its current text follows) and return it WHOLE; change only the bodies of guardrailRules and cardRules (and the Unit interface, which gains `files: string[]`), every export, signature, type, import, message and order stays as it is. In guardrailRules each unit also keeps its code files: codeTargets(profile, targets), distinct, in order (codeTargets is already imported). Then, for each canonical name: a place starting with "Function " or "Interface " writes its text to the key of each code file of the unit (create rules[file] = {} when it is missing), a place starting with "Component " or "System " to the key of each dir of the unit, as today; in both the first text for an id wins (Object.hasOwn). Every dir stays a key; the final sort walks every key. In cardRules, per dir d (first seen first) build a new object: for each code target t in d, in target order, each id of rules[t] (when Object.hasOwn(rules, t)) not yet set; then each id of rules[d] (when Object.hasOwn(rules, d)) not yet set; then copy it with its keys sorted (Object.keys(o).sort()). Pure: no file read, no clock, no environment, no process. Write no test file: a probe tests you and a judge writes the example tests.

## Function Guardrail Rules

For every code directory of the record, the guard rule ids its canonical Guardrails give, and the names that stay prose (P31a, issue

Behaviour: guardrailRules(record, map) → Guardrail Rules Result, over the WHOLE record and map (never a cut's subset). Per Component C in record order: profile = Resolve Profile(C.language, map.language), an error → "Component '<C>': <it>" and C is skipped. C's units, in order: each Function F of C, then each Interface I of C whose exposes does not hold exactly one name. A unit's targets: for F as in Layer Edges (the first map group holding F's name gives the unit name, else F's name; the targets of the map card whose id is slugName(unit name) when that card gives targets, else [code, test] of Name Targets(profile, C.name, unit name)); for I the map card slugName(I.name) when it gives targets, else [code, test] of Name Targets(profile, C.name, I.name); a Name Targets error → "Component '<C>': <it>". The unit's dirs = path.posix.dirname of each of codeTargets(profile, targets) ("." for a root file), distinct; every dir is a key of rules (an object, {} when no rule falls on it). The unit's names, in order, each with its place: for F, F.guardrails ("Function <F.name>"), then the guardrails (`?? []`) of every Interface of C whose exposes is exactly [F.name] ("Interface <I.name>"), in C's order; for I, I's guardrails ("Interface <I.name>"); then C.guardrails ("Component <C.name>"); then record.system.guardrails ("System <system name>"). Per name N: id = Canonical Guardrail's guardrailRule(profile, N); null → N joins proseOnly unless a name with the same guardrailKey is already in it; else the text "Guardrail '<N>' of <place>" goes, unless the key already has id (the first place, the most specific, wins), to: for a Function or Interface place, the key f of each code file f of codeTargets(profile, targets) of the unit (the file key is created, as {}, when its first rule falls on it: a code file with no Function or Interface rule is no key); for a Component or System place, the key d of each dir of the unit. So a Function's rule never reaches a sibling card's file of its directory. Any error → {ok: false, errors} (record order, each text once); else {ok: true, rules, proseOnly}: the keys of rules and of each entry sorted ascending by code unit (new objects built in that order; a dir sorts before its files), proseOnly in first-seen order, each name as written. Data Object, Event and Actor guardrails are not read.

Steps:
- reads: Contour Record
- reads: Contour Map
- uses: contour
- uses: language
- produces: Guardrail Rules Result

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given the record and the map of tests/fixtures/rules/parity/go/ (contour.yaml, morph-map.json: calc, clock and shell carry the Guardrail Pure, app none); when guardrailRules; then {ok: true, rules: {"app": {}, "calc": {"pure": "Guardrail 'Pure' of Component calc"}, "clock": {"pure": "Guardrail 'Pure' of Component clock"}, "shell": {"pure": "Guardrail 'Pure' of Component shell"}}, proseOnly: []} (ref: tests/fixtures/rules/parity/go/contour.yaml, tests/fixtures/rules/parity/go/morph-map.json)
2. given examples.json["Guardrail Rules 2"].given; when guardrailRules; then examples.json["Guardrail Rules 2"].then (ref: tests/fixtures/rules/examples.json, tests/fixtures/rules/parity/typescript/contour.yaml, tests/fixtures/rules/parity/typescript/morph-map.json)
3. given examples.json["Guardrail Rules 3"].given; when guardrailRules; then examples.json["Guardrail Rules 3"].then (ref: tests/fixtures/rules/examples.json, tests/fixtures/rules/guarded.yaml)
4. given the record tests/fixtures/rules/badLanguage.yaml (Component legacy, language cobol; Component fresh, go; System Pure) and the empty map; when guardrailRules; then {ok: false, errors: ["Component 'legacy': unknown language 'cobol' (known: typescript, python, go)"]} (ref: tests/fixtures/rules/badLanguage.yaml)
5. given examples.json["Guardrail Rules 5"].given; when guardrailRules; then examples.json["Guardrail Rules 5"].then (ref: tests/fixtures/rules/examples.json, tests/fixtures/rules/scope/cases.json)

Data Contour Record: The typed record (src/contour/types.ts); every list present, every optional text null when absent, texts trimmed.
Schema:
{ version: 1, system: { name, description, requirements: string[], guardrails: string[], groups: Component[], dependencies: Dependency[] }, actors: { name, description, uses: string[], requirements, guardrails }[], requirements: { name, description }[], guardrails: { name, description }[] }; Dependency = { name, version, language, doc: string | null }; Component = { name, description, language: string | null, requirements, guardrails, uses: string[], functions: { name, description, behavior ("" when absent), requirements, guardrails, preconditions: string[], steps: { verb: 'calls'|'reads'|'modifies'|'produces'|'uses', target }[], examples: { given, when, then, ref: string | null }[] }[], dataObjects: { name, description, schema: string | null, requirements, guardrails }[], interfaces: { name, description, exposes: string[], requirements?, guardrails?, schema?: string | null }[], events: { name, description, requirements, guardrails, schema: string | null }[], references, consumes, dependsOn: string[] }; the three Interface fields are optional in the type (an Interface built by hand in an older test still compiles) and always set by Validate Record

Data Contour Map: The typed map; snake_case keys of the document become camelCase fields, a key the map does not set is null.
Schema:
{ version: 1, package: string | null, language: string | null, docs: string[], groups: { name, functions: string[] }[], cards: ({ id } & CardFields)[], extraCards: ({ component: string | null } & CardFields)[] }; CardFields = { customId, intent: 'generate'|'patch', targets, contextSlice, dependsOn, instruction, acceptance, model, maxTokens, reasoningMaxTokens, variants }, each | null

Data Guardrail Rules Result: Every code directory of the record with its rule ids and their texts, and the names that stay prose; or every error.
Schema:
{ ok: true, rules: Record<string, Record<string, string>>, proseOnly: string[] } | { ok: false, errors: string[] }

## Function Card Rules

The part of the rules one card's guard gets — its code directories.

Behaviour: cardRules(profile, targets, rules) → an object: for each directory d of codeTargets(profile, targets) (path.posix.dirname, "." for a root file; distinct, first seen first, so the keys keep that order) the entry d → a new object: first, for each code target t of the card in d, in target order, every id of rules[t] (own key t) not yet in it; then every id of rules[d] (own key d) not yet in it (the file's rule, the more specific, wins); its keys sorted ascending (default sort). No code target → {}. The contract-3 guard reads its rules by directory and is given only this card's code files, so the entry of d is the rule set of each of the card's files in d: the System and Component rules of d plus this card's Function and Interface rules, never a sibling card's.

Steps:
- reads: Guardrail Rules Result
- produces: Record<string, Record<string, string>>

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given RG = the rules of Guardrail Rules example 1, RT = those of example 3; cardRules(go, ["calc/add.go", "calc/add_test.go"], RG); cardRules(typescript, ["src/orders/placeOrder.ts", "tests/orders/placeOrder.test.ts"], RT); cardRules(go, ["new/a.go", "new/b.go", "main.go"], {}); cardRules(go, ["calc/add_examples_test.go"], RG); when cardRules; then {"calc": RG["calc"]}; {"src/orders": {"no-clock": "Guardrail 'no CLOCK' of Component orders", "no-network": "Guardrail 'No Network' of System guarded", "no-shell": "Guardrail 'No Shell' of Function Place Order"}} (its dir and its file, not the sibling cards' files); {"new": {}, ".": {}} with the keys in that order; {}
2. given examples.json["Card Rules 2"].given; when cardRules; then examples.json["Card Rules 2"].then (ref: tests/fixtures/rules/examples.json)

Data Guardrail Rules Result: Every code directory of the record with its rule ids and their texts, and the names that stay prose; or every error.
Schema:
{ ok: true, rules: Record<string, Record<string, string>>, proseOnly: string[] } | { ok: false, errors: string[] }

## Function Rules Arg

The guard's rules argument, after the layers argument of Layers Arg.

Behaviour: rulesArg(rules) → string. rules undefined → "" (the guard line stays byte for byte). Else " '" + JSON.stringify(rules), every "'" in it written as the six characters \u0027 (the shell word stays single-quoted; JSON reads it back as '), + "'". It is written right after Layers Arg, so the guard reads it as the fifth argument of `src`. The template guards of contract 3 (templates/go and templates/typescript decks/tools/guard.mjs, the line "// morph-guard-contract: 3"; data) take `src <files> <mods> <layers> <rules>`: a missing layers argument → exit 1 and "guard: no layer edges given — re-cut with morph plan", a missing rules argument → "guard: no Guardrail rules given — re-cut with morph plan" (fail closed, never "everything allowed": issue #46); no file beside the record is read (P31b: decks/tools/layers.json not at all, TypeScript's packages come from the `pkgs` argument only, the record's dependencies of the card's Component). Per given code file (Go: never a _test.go) the rules of its directory, as each guard's header lists them (no-shell, no-clock, no-network, no-env, no-process for TypeScript only, stdlib-only, pure), are checked on the syntax tree (Go: a go/parser scan run by `go run` in a temporary module; TypeScript: its compiler API); each finding is one line "guard: <file>:<line>: imports <path>|uses <name>: <the rule's text>", for the first rule in that order that forbids it. P31b (#42 Must hold 3, #40 item 3): imports are checked per given code file too, never per package — an import no rule forbids is allowed when it is of the standard library, of the module (then the layer rule of Layers Arg) or of the `mods`/`pkgs` argument; any other is one line, Go "guard: <file>:<line>: imports <path>: not a dependency the record gives this Component (allowed: the standard library[, <mods joined by ', '>])", TypeScript as before ("guard: <file>:<line> package import \"<spec>\" (allowed: node:*[, <pkgs>])"). Only the card's own files are read, so a package-mate's import is never its red: Blame Log blames the card whose acceptance it is, the owner of the named file.

Steps:
- produces: string

## Function Guard Contract

The contract number a project guard declares.

Behaviour: guardContract(guard) → number: the digits of the first match of /morph-guard-contract: (\d+)/ in the guard's text, as a number; no match → 0 (a hand guard, or a template copy older than P30).

Steps:
- produces: number

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given guardContract("// guard\n"); guardContract("// morph-guard-contract: 2\n"); guardContract("x\n// morph-guard-contract: 3\n// morph-guard-contract: 2\n"); guardContract("// morph-guard-contract: x\n"); when guardContract; then 0; 2; 3; 0

## Function Plan Rules

What `plan --checks` gives the builder — layers and rules when the project guard speaks their contract (P31a, issues

Behaviour: planRules(record, map, layersFile, guard, language) → Plan Rules Result. n = Guard Contract(guard). n < 2 and layersFile false → {ok: true, layers: null, rules: null, proseOnly: []}, nothing else read (a hand guard: MorphV2's own, every deck byte for byte). Else layers = Plan Layers(record, map, true, n ≥ 2 ? GUARD_CONTRACT : guard, language) (so a guard of contract 2 or more gets the record's edges whether decks/tools/layers.json exists or not, issue #46; an older copy beside a layers.json is refused as in P30), its error → {ok: false, error: it}; then Guardrail Rules(record, map), errors → {ok: false, error: them joined by "\n"}. n ≥ 3 → {ok: true, layers: its layers, rules, proseOnly}. Else, when some key of rules (a directory or a file) has a rule → {ok: false, error: "decks/tools/guard.mjs speaks contract <n, at least 1>: copy templates/<language>/decks/tools/guard.mjs from MorphV2"} (an older guard would ignore the rules); else {ok: true, layers: its layers, rules: null, proseOnly: []}.

Steps:
- calls: Guard Contract
- calls: Guardrail Rules
- uses: rules
- produces: Plan Rules Result

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Write the files: `src/rules/guardrails.ts`.

TypeScript with `strict` on, ESM with NodeNext resolution: every relative import carries the `.js` extension and types are imported with `import type`. No `any`: use `unknown` and narrow. Tests are vitest: `toBe` on scalars and short strings, `toStrictEqual` on a whole result; stubs come from `tests/helpers.ts`, never your own.

You write two test files and return each WHOLE. (1) tests/rules/guardrails.examples.test.ts (its current text follows): change only two tests. In "Guardrail Rules example 3" the expected rules become the five keys of docs/TASK_P31c_scope.md section 2.2 (catalog as now; "src/orders" with no-clock and no-network only; "src/orders/cancelOrder.ts" with no-process and pure; "src/orders/ordersApi.ts" with no-env; "src/orders/placeOrder.ts" with no-shell; the texts verbatim), proseOnly as now. In "Card Rules example 1" the second expectation becomes {"src/orders": {"no-clock": "Guardrail 'no  CLOCK' of Component orders", "no-network": "Guardrail 'No Network' of System guarded", "no-shell": "Guardrail 'No Shell' of Function Place Order"}}. Change nothing else in that file: every test, its name and every other expectation kept (14 tests). (2) tests/rules/guardrails.p31c.examples.test.ts, a NEW file: one test per example of Guardrail Rules 5, Card Rules 2 and Rules Arg 8 (3 tests in that order, named "<Function> example <N>: <what>"); the given and then of each are in tests/fixtures/rules/examples.json (in your slice). The fixture rules/scope/cases.json is {go, typescript} each {map: string (the map's JSON text), tree: Record<string, string>, files: Record<string, string> (code file to card id), records: Record<string, string> (record texts: function, interface, component, system), then: Record<string, Record<string, {status: number, stdout: string}>>}; read it with fixtureJson and a cast. Guardrail Rules 5 loads the records with loadContour(text, "contour.yaml") and the map with loadMap(text, "morph-map.json") (each returns {ok, record} / {ok, map}; throw when not ok). Card Rules 2 uses GO and keeps the literals of its given verbatim; check the key order of the first result with Object.keys. Rules Arg 8 is the harness of section 2.1 verbatim: two loops (language, record key), then the files; every run in a fresh tmp root; {status, stdout} toStrictEqual then[K][file]; a test timeout of 240000 ms. Import guardrailRules, cardRules, planRules from "../../src/rules/guardrails.js", loadContour and loadMap from "../../src/contour/load.js", GO and TYPESCRIPT from "../../src/language/profiles.js", fixtureJson, fixturePath and tmpRoot from "../helpers.js", spawnSync from "node:child_process", fs from "node:fs", path from "node:path". Strings with toBe, a whole result with toStrictEqual; a literal holding a single quote goes in a double-quoted string. Every tmp root is removed in finally (r.rm()). No vi.mock, vi.stubGlobal, vi.useFakeTimers, no timer (setTimeout, setInterval, setImmediate), no function or variable named fetch or Fake*. Import only what you use; eslint rejects an unused import or constant and a `let` never reassigned; import test and expect from "vitest".

Data Contour Record: The typed record (src/contour/types.ts); every list present, every optional text null when absent, texts trimmed.
Schema:
{ version: 1, system: { name, description, requirements: string[], guardrails: string[], groups: Component[], dependencies: Dependency[] }, actors: { name, description, uses: string[], requirements, guardrails }[], requirements: { name, description }[], guardrails: { name, description }[] }; Dependency = { name, version, language, doc: string | null }; Component = { name, description, language: string | null, requirements, guardrails, uses: string[], functions: { name, description, behavior ("" when absent), requirements, guardrails, preconditions: string[], steps: { verb: 'calls'|'reads'|'modifies'|'produces'|'uses', target }[], examples: { given, when, then, ref: string | null }[] }[], dataObjects: { name, description, schema: string | null, requirements, guardrails }[], interfaces: { name, description, exposes: string[], requirements?, guardrails?, schema?: string | null }[], events: { name, description, requirements, guardrails, schema: string | null }[], references, consumes, dependsOn: string[] }; the three Interface fields are optional in the type (an Interface built by hand in an older test still compiles) and always set by Validate Record

Data Contour Map: The typed map; snake_case keys of the document become camelCase fields, a key the map does not set is null.
Schema:
{ version: 1, package: string | null, language: string | null, docs: string[], groups: { name, functions: string[] }[], cards: ({ id } & CardFields)[], extraCards: ({ component: string | null } & CardFields)[] }; CardFields = { customId, intent: 'generate'|'patch', targets, contextSlice, dependsOn, instruction, acceptance, model, maxTokens, reasoningMaxTokens, variants }, each | null

Data Guardrail Rules Result: Every code directory of the record with its rule ids and their texts, and the names that stay prose; or every error.
Schema:
{ ok: true, rules: Record<string, Record<string, string>>, proseOnly: string[] } | { ok: false, errors: string[] }

Data Plan Rules Result: The layers and rules for the builder (each null when the guard does not speak its contract) and the prose-only names, or the one error.
Schema:
{ ok: true, layers: Record<string, string[]> | null, rules: Record<string, Record<string, string>> | null, proseOnly: string[] } | { ok: false, error: string }
